cohort: 125 multiparous women with recurrent preeclampsia and 742 multiparous women with a first episode of preeclampsia
finding: Recurrent preeclamptic women had a higher risk of prior chronic hypertension and early onset preeclampsia, and their newborns were more likely to have very low birth weight.
mod_finding: Women with recurrent preeclampsia were more likely to have C-sections, suggesting a potential association with mode of birth.
gest_age: 34.1 weeks for recurrent preeclampsia group, 34.7 weeks for first preeclampsia group
birth_weight: Very low birth weight (< 1500 g) was more common in newborns of mothers with recurrent preeclampsia
